summary.intent: Review and refine a PR adding an `entire attach` command for importing existing agent sessions into Entire's checkpoint/commit tracking system.
summary.outcome: Review completed with several issues addressed: a comment clarifying strategy coupling, error messaging improved for auto-detection failures, depth calculation in transcript search replaced with filepath.Rel, and no-arg behavior fixed to show help instead of bare error. One open UX question about re-attaching already-tracked sessions was raised but not resolved.

repo: root.go:39 sets SilenceUsage: true globally, so cobra.ExactArgs validation errors never show usage/help text — commands needing help-on-no-args must handle it manually in RunE
GetStrategy() already returns *strategy.ManualCommitStrategy (concrete type), so the coupling to ManualCommitStrategy is pervasive, not isolated to condenseAndFinalizeSession

CondenseSessionByID calls five private methods on the strategy receiver (loadSessionState, CondenseSession, clearSessionState, saveSessionState, cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused), making it hard to extract to a package-level function without a larger refactor
Checkpoint storage is conceptually strategy-independent but currently lives on the strategy struct — acknowledged as known tech debt

IsTrailerLine regex (^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*: ) has known false positives (e.g. 'error: connection refused') but is only called in AppendCheckpointTrailer with blank-line-above context, preventing real bugs
promptAmendCommit failure is already handled gracefully — falls back to printing the trailer for manual copy

code.finding: Guard blocks any session that already has a state file; valid re-attach scenarios (session tracked but commit missing Entire-Checkpoint trailer) are not supported
Error now includes both original agent error and auto-detection failure for clearer user messaging
condenseAndFinalizeSession takes *strategy.ManualCommitStrategy directly; comment updated to explain checkpoint storage is coupled to strategy struct and what a fix would require
Replaced strings.Count(filepath.Separator) depth arithmetic with filepath.Rel for correctness across path normalization edge cases
exec.CommandContext for git commit --amend; GPG signing and pre-commit hooks behave as configured by user, failures fall back to manual trailer copy

workflow: When cobra.ExactArgs is used with SilenceUsage:true, handle missing args in RunE with cmd.Help() + return nil to show help instead of a bare error
filepath.Rel is more robust than counting path separators for depth checks in WalkDir traversal
Speculative refactoring (extracting to interfaces, package-level functions) should be deferred until a second concrete use case exists

friction: Repeated reads of the same large tool-result file (bag4ea9w2.txt) suggest the diff was too large to hold in context, requiring multiple re-reads to locate specific sections
ExactArgs + SilenceUsage:true is a global footgun that silently breaks help-on-no-args for all commands — discovered only after a user hit the bad UX in production
open_items: Re-attach UX: `entire attach` on an already-tracked session should support linking an existing checkpoint to a commit (amend with trailer) without re-running the full attach flow — design not finalized
Checkpoint storage is conceptually strategy-independent but lives on ManualCommitStrategy; extraction deferred until a second strategy is needed
Other commands (e.g. resume.go) have the same ExactArgs + SilenceUsage:true no-help-on-missing-args issue — only attach.go was fixed
attach_test.go: TestAttach_CursorSuccess and TestAttach_FactoryAIDroidSuccess are nearly identical and could be table-driven — deferred as a nit
